 Forget Rodrygo, Arsenal’s next winger target is blindingly obvious 
 Arsenal have been linked to Real Madrid winger Rodrygo By Dylan Oakley | Nov 17, 2026, 11:15 AM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Real Madrid Training Session | Antonio Villalba/GettyImages As we get closer to the January transfer window, reports of potential incomings at Arsenal are growing. The Gunners made a few good additions in the summer, such as Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, and Ezri Konsa, but they'll now be focusing on how they can improve even more. 
--> As we get closer to the January transfer window, reports of potential incomings at Arsenal are growing. The Gunners made a few good additions in the summer, such as Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, and Ezri Konsa, but they'll now be focusing on how they can improve even more. 
 The left winger position remains a topic of debate. Tzolis hasn't exactly claimed the spot amid inconsistent form and injury struggles, and aside from him, Eberechi Eze has struggled , and Noni Madueke's natural position remains on the right. 
--> The left winger position remains a topic of debate. Tzolis hasn't exactly claimed the spot amid inconsistent form and injury struggles, and aside from him, Eberechi Eze has struggled , and Noni Madueke's natural position remains on the right. 
 Arsenal may decide to add a left-winger in January so they can finally have their long-term replacement for both Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard, who both left in the summer transfer window. 
--> Arsenal may decide to add a left-winger in January so they can finally have their long-term replacement for both Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard, who both left in the summer transfer window. 
 Arsenal remain linked with Rodrygo
--> Arsenal remain linked with Rodrygo
 They've been linked with Real Madrid winger Rodrygo , who is yet to play this season because of injury. He had been dealing with an ACL injury that he suffered in March of last year. He's getting close to a return, as he's now back in training, and amid his impending return, reports have linked him yet again with a potential move to the Emirates. 
--> They've been linked with Real Madrid winger Rodrygo , who is yet to play this season because of injury. He had been dealing with an ACL injury that he suffered in March of last year. He's getting close to a return, as he's now back in training, and amid his impending return, reports have linked him yet again with a potential move to the Emirates. 
 It'd be a risky move for the Gunners, as the 25-year-old has had a rocky history with injuries over the past few years. He's only played 19 league games since the start of last season, and there's no guarantee that his luck would turn if he came to North London. 
--> It'd be a risky move for the Gunners, as the 25-year-old has had a rocky history with injuries over the past few years. He's only played 19 league games since the start of last season, and there's no guarantee that his luck would turn if he came to North London. 
 Furthermore, his cost would be extortionate. Last year, he was linked with a move to the Premier League, and reports were claiming that a transfer fee of £80 million plus could be enough to land him. Granted, his market value has likely dropped since then, but even so, Real Madrid would drive a hard bargain, and so the Gunners would potentially have to overspend on an injury-prone player, should they go after him.

 Arsenal should target Antonio Nusa instead
--> Arsenal should target Antonio Nusa instead
 In terms of other targets, Antonio Nusa seems to be an obvious choice over someone like Rodrygo for Arsenal, as he makes a lot more sense. The Norwegian winger, for a start, does not have a turbulent injury history, nor does he have the big-name price tag attached to him. 
--> In terms of other targets, Antonio Nusa seems to be an obvious choice over someone like Rodrygo for Arsenal, as he makes a lot more sense. The Norwegian winger, for a start, does not have a turbulent injury history, nor does he have the big-name price tag attached to him. 
 Nusa has been linked with Arsenal recently, as the RB Leipzig forward has been one of the best attackers in the Bundesliga this year. He's already scored four goals and provided seven assists in nine games - think of the damage he could do alongside the likes of Bukayo Saka , Kai Havertz or Viktor Gyokeres...

 Furthermore, the 20-year-old is still developing, considering he's already breaking out like this at 20, think how good he could be in five years' time - it would really be a long-term investment. Also, Nusa already has ties to Arsenal in the form of Martin Odegaard.

 Norwegian football is certainly in it's golden age at the moment, and Odegaard and Nusa are part of the reason why. They both start for Norway, and are two of the nation's best stars, having already developed a partnership together, making any move to Arsenal even smoother.
